newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks stage rebound in early Monday trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks stage rebound in early Monday trade.

text.p: French shares rebounded on Monday from Friday's sharp fall, tracking a rise in bonds after European Union leaders agreed on a stability pact to enforce budget discipline once a single European currency is introduced.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 19.67 points or 0.89 percent at 2,223.08 at 1015 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was 20 points higher at 2,230.

Traders expect the market to move cautiously ahead of the Bank of France's annual news conference on Tuesday, the Federal Open Market Committee meeting this week and the Bundesbank's council meeting on Thursday.
Shares in luxury goods group LVMH rose 1.43 percent to 1,276 francs. One analyst said the stock's rise was partly technical, as it had fallen sharply on Friday.
But she said the stock was also underpinned by talk that the company's proposed acquisition of U.S. duty free chain DFS would close before the end of the year.
Japan's move after the World Trade Organisation meeting in Singapore to study ways to narrow the gap between tax on domestic and imported spirits is also seen as positive for LVMH.
